Ph.D. Dissertation Research  ·  Working Analytical Tool

Interpretable Network Metrics for Equity-Aware Prioritization of Bridge Rehabilitation and Recovery

Weight & Influencing-Factor Sensitivity Tool

InstitutionFlorida International University (FIU)
DepartmentMoss School of Construction
Faculty AdvisorDr. Walied Orabi, Associate Professor

An interactive instrument for testing how factor weighting and the inclusion of candidate influencing factors change bridge rehabilitation priority rankings across New York State — built directly from the Master Factor Matrix (Sheet 3) and Factor Operationalization sheet (Sheet 6) of the five-state bridge prioritization workbook.

Applied to the full NY-04 statewide bridge panel — 17,532 structures (Sheet 15, NYSDOT / data.ny.gov, pulled 2026-09-04)

On the data underneath this tool. Condition (Poor Status), Region, County, Owner, and Age are real, sourced values drawn from the NY-04 panel. AADT, Truck %, Detour, Scour, Fracture-Critical, Material Risk, and the Equity Index are illustrative placeholder values — the workbook itself notes (Sheets 6 and 14) that these are not yet joined to real New York bridge records. They are simulated here, deterministically, so the mechanics of weighting and factor inclusion can be tested before real data is available. Substituting real figures for the placeholder columns requires no change to the tool's structure or formulas.

Distribution & Regional Composition

Composite score distribution

Composite score distribution across all 17,532 bridges. The shaded band marks the top-25 cutoff under the current weighting.

Regional composition of top 25

NYSDOT region of origin for the current top 25, against each region's statewide share (grey tick) for reference.

Composite score = weighted sum of within-panel percentile ranks (0–100 scale) across active factors, following the normalization approach noted in Sheet 6. This is a demonstration of prioritization mechanics, not a validated model — rankings should be treated as illustrative until real AADT, detour, scour, and fracture-criticality data are joined to the NY panel, per the task list in Sheet 14.
